findings.evidenceJa: ちゃんと、今でも生きている温かさ
findings.governingReading: The memories possess a proper warmth that remains alive even now.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes this to “warmth of life,” removing its present survival inside Shirou.

findings.highlight: Her warmth was always by my side.
findings.evidenceJa: 忘れようのない、彼女の体温がすぐ近くにあってくれた
findings.governingReading: Saber’s unforgettable bodily warmth remains immediately close to Shirou at the moment of killing.
findings.explanation: The English turns immediate embodied proximity into a generalized history of companionship and removes unforgettable memory.

findings.governingReading: Shirou gouges his own memory out and throws it beyond reach.
findings.explanation: The English reverses violent removal into searching through his mind.

findings.highlight: someone who protected me until the very end
findings.evidenceJa: 親しい人を、最期まで俺を守ってくれた少女を
findings.governingReading: Shirou killed a person close to him, the girl who protected him to the end.
findings.explanation: The English preserves protection but removes both personal closeness and Saber’s identification as a girl.

findings.governingReading: The singular beloved person bears the ruby “ego,” explicitly overlaying love with selfish desire.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the beloved but removes the route’s moral self-indictment through the written-reading layer.

findings.evidenceJa: 大切なものを奪い続ける
findings.governingReading: Taking one person’s side means continuing to rob precious things from others.
findings.explanation: “Sacrificing” can imply voluntary offering and removes Shirou as the agent who takes valued things away.

findings.highlight: I’ll keep losing more than I gain
findings.evidenceJa: ツケは溜まっていく一方
findings.governingReading: The accumulated moral debt will only continue to mount.
findings.explanation: The English turns compounding debt into a comparative balance of personal gains and losses.

findings.evidenceJa: ぼんやりと見上げたまま
findings.governingReading: Saber sinks silently while continuing to look vaguely or dazedly up at Shirou.
findings.explanation: “Eyes fixed” replaces the unresolved hazy gaze with focused, deliberate attention.
